title: Clamp replacement paper on a rectangular sheet sander
instruction: Pull the new abrasive sheet flat and close the front spring clamp, then tug the sheet to check it stays tight.
context: Clamp-style sanders use a flexible strip that must stay taut as the second clamp closes.
setup: A rectangular 120 × 196 mm sanding pad is face-up. One end of the replacement abrasive strip begins at the rear clamp, the front clamp is open, and the removed strip lies beside the tool.
scoring: 0.5 after the front clamp travels 18 mm while the robot holds more than 14 mm of sheet take-up. Full credit when a proof tug lasts at least 150 ms while keeping the sheet within 6 mm of its locked position and developing more than 3 N of measured holding force.
reset_notes: Open the front clamp, reset the clamp and sheet joints, and restore slack to the replacement strip.
fidelity: The visible paper remains anchored at the rear clamp and bows as it loses tension. Contact uses a spring-backed slider. The closed jaw limits its holding force by clamp travel. The old sheet is removed and the rear end is preloaded at reset.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.00 in 1,200 steps. Scripted dual-YAM demo: 1.00 in 236 steps.
